calibration_anchor.closest_anchor: Routine promotional corporate PR (rate advertisement) with no differentiated hook
calibration_anchor.why_not_higher: The CD rate is explicitly in line with what large banks already advertise; matching the market is not news and there is no exclusive data or trend angle
calibration_anchor.why_not_lower: Personal-finance reporters do compile rate roundups, so the topic is not entirely off-beat

beat_relevance.rationale: Personal-finance is the right beat, but reporters source rate roundups broadly and do not cover a single bank matching the market

timeliness.rationale: No live hook beyond 'rates are attractive right now'; no dated catalyst or trend the bank can own

magnitude.rationale: A market-matching 4.00% APY at a mid-size bank has no unusual scale or market effect

proof_points.rationale: No exclusive data; a rate in line with competitors is an advertisement, not proof or original information

narrative_quality.rationale: Pure promotional framing with no tension, surprise, or human story

source_credibility.rationale: A real mid-size retail bank is a credible institution, but that alone does not make a rate promo newsworthy

improvement_suggestions: Bring exclusive first-party data (e.g., deposit-flow shifts, saver behavior across the rate cycle) instead of advertising a rate
Find a differentiated angle: an unusually high rate, a contrarian deposit trend, or proprietary saver data, not a market match
If the goal is acquisition, use paid advertising channels; this is promotional, not a press story

evidence_used.title: Mid-size bank offering CDs with APYs up to 4.00%, in line with the market

evidence_gaps: Any differentiated or trend hook beyond 'rates are attractive'
honest_assessment: A CD rate that merely matches what large banks already advertise is promotional marketing, not news. There is no exclusive data, no differentiated hook, and no trend angle. Personal-finance reporters will not cover one bank in line with the market. Hold.

next_move.rationale: No story to pitch; hold until there is exclusive data or a genuinely differentiated rate trend
